name: Relevant solutions named, recall first
purpose: Measures whether, for a change, a candidate or a request, every solution that needed its own consideration is named, and how few that did not, at what cost: on cases mined from a repository's history (a commit's subject in, the solutions whose code it changed out) and hand-labelled cases for requests, outside candidates and bug reports, with a held-out share.
record: Per arm, cases passed (every gold solution returned and at least a quarter of the chosen solutions gold) out of cases run, with mean recall, mean precision and the cases that missed a solution in the details; the balanced score with [balance.solution_relevance] (accuracy 0.7, cost 0.15, time 0.15, fixed before any arm was scored).
disadvantages: A commit subject is shorter and more technical than a request; a commit that changed a file for an unrelated reason labels a solution that did not need consideration; the hand-labelled cases are few. The pass rule (every gold solution and a precision floor) lets a tighter cut pass more cases while mean recall falls, so mean recall in the details is read beside the pass count, and a recall term of its own is the next refinement of the number.
cascading_conditionals: free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the free arms classify every mined and hand-labelled case of this repository: seconds] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=a cheap model classifier arm exists and a person approved its budget: one case end to end] > sample [sample=sample:10 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=the model arm passed its one case: ten cases, then thirty] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | when=the model arm leads on the sample and a person approved the budget]
command: esoi run solution_relevance --impl index_with_links; esoi run solution_relevance --impl lexical_index
